A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEDIC-AD and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. All 13 pages of each version support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection, temporal-reasoning, visual-grounding, clinical-data, and ablation results, including additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the clinical evaluation on 300 patients and supplementary benchmark and ablation results.

M1.justification: The three-stage framework, anomaly and difference tokens, Q-Formers, heatmap decoder, training objectives, and chat template are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged, including anomaly detection, MMXU, visual grounding, the 300-patient clinical dataset, and medical VQA/QA benchmarks in Appendix C.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments, including Citrus-V for grounding, Lingshu for the clinical evaluation, and fully fine-tuned Lingshu in the supplementary comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C retain the same evaluation prompts, metrics, model sizes, clinical sample size, training budgets, and experimental configurations.

E4.justification: The anomaly-token and layer-selection ablations, pooling and soft-prompt sensitivity analyses, qualitative examples, and stage-wise versus joint-training comparison are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match, including supplementary results. For example, MEDIC-AD retains 91.6 average F1 in Table 1 and 0.655 overall MMXU accuracy in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) and the associated mathematical formulations are identical. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about lesion detection, temporal reasoning, visual explainability, benchmark superiority, and clinical applicability.

C2.justification: Interpretations of anomaly-token benefits, temporal reasoning, clinical reliability, and knowledge retention remain unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Appendix B's hardware, training times, optimizer, hyperparameters, and module sizes remain unchanged, as does the code URL. The new GPU-support acknowledgement supplies funding attribution rather than additional technical settings or access instructions.

R1.justification: All 68 references and the related-work discussion are retained. References move within pages because of the new acknowledgements, without changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgements section listing grants, institutional support, and J. Do's ASRI affiliation, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgements reflow references across pages 9–11, and page 8 has small spacing and conclusion line-wrap changes. All six figures and ten tables retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding and institutional attribution but leaves the scientific exposition, evidence, reproducibility details, claims, and appendices unchanged. The limited layout adjustments produce no material readability gain or harm, so the revision does not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
